transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling deeply depressed, sad, and empty inside for about nine months now. I've also completely lost interest in the things I used to enjoy doing. It has just become really hard to keep going like this.
Have you ever experienced periods lasting a few days where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or needed much less sleep than normal, even if you currently feel depressed?

Yes, before this depression hit, I had a period of about five months where I felt the exact opposite. I had endless energy, talked constantly, and barely slept at all without ever feeling tired. It was completely different from how empty and exhausted I feel now.
During that five-month period of high energy, did you require hospitalization, or did your symptoms cause such severe impairment that you were unable to function at work or in your social life?
I'm not really sure if it was serious enough to need hospital care. I was definitely very active and doing a lot, but I'm not sure if it caused severe impairment in my work or social life back then.
During that high-energy period, did you ever experience any unusual beliefs that were not based in reality, or hear or see things that other people could not?
No, I never experienced anything like that. I didn't hear or see things that weren't there, and I didn't have any unusual beliefs.

During that five-month period of high energy, did you feel like you were acting in a way that was clearly different from your usual self to the extent that others around you—like family, friends, or coworkers—definitely noticed a change in your behavior?

Yes, people around me definitely noticed a major change in my behavior during those five months. My family and friends kept pointing out how incredibly talkative and unusually social I had become. Even my coworkers noticed that I was suddenly starting and driving far more projects than normal at work.

Did this change in your behavior cause any significant problems or conflicts in your personal or professional life, or were you still able to manage your responsibilities effectively during that time?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't thought much about whether those changes caused any specific conflicts or how well I was actually managing my responsibilities at the time.

Looking back, do you recall if that period of high energy resulted in any reckless or impulsive actions, such as excessive spending, risky sexual behavior, or making impulsive decisions that you later regretted?

During that time, I did have a significantly increased interest and activity regarding sex. However, I don't recall doing any reckless spending or making other major impulsive decisions that I regretted.

Was there ever a time during those five months where your behavior or the intensity of your actions caused a clear, noticeable disruption in your ability to hold down your job or maintain your important relationships?

Actually, rather than causing disruptions, it felt like the opposite because I was taking on so many more projects at work than usual. I was also extremely social and actively reaching out to people, so I didn't see it as a failure to manage my job or relationships at the time.

Since you were still able to function well at work and in your relationships during that five-month period, would you say the changes in your mood and energy were noticeable to others, even if they didn't lead to a total breakdown in your daily life?

Yes, the changes were definitely very noticeable to everyone around me. My family and friends kept commenting on how fast I was talking and how unusually social and chatty I had become. Even my coworkers pointed out that I was taking on an intense amount of work and projects all at once.
